verses.text: When dem draw near to Jerusalem, and come to Bethsphage, to di Mount of Olives, den Jesus send two disciples,
and talk say to dem, “Go enter di village wey dey opposite una, and immediately una go find donkey wey dem tie, and young donkey with am. Untie dem, and bring dem to me.”
“If anybody talk anything to una, una go talk say, ‘Lord need dem,’ and immediately e go send dem.”
Dis happen so that wetin dem talk through di prophet go dey fulfilled, wey talk say,
“Tell Zion daughter, ‘Look, your King dey come to you, humble, dey ride donkey, even young donkey, di foal of donkey.’”
Di disciples leave, and do just as Jesus command dem,
and bring di donkey and di young donkey, and lay dem clothes on dem; and e sit on dem.
Very great multitude spread dem clothes for di road. Others cut branches from di trees, and spread dem for di road.
Di multitudes wey go before am, and wey follow, dey shout, “Hosanna to David pikin! Blessed na di one wey dey come for di name of di Lord! Hosanna for di highest!”
When e don enter Jerusalem, all di city dey stirred up, dey talk say, “Who be dis?”
Di multitudes talk say, “Dis na di prophet, Jesus, from Nazareth of Galilee.”
Jesus enter di temple of God and drive out all dem wey dey sell and buy for di temple, and overthrow di money changers tables and di seats of dem wey dey sell doves.
E talk say to dem, “Dem write am, ‘My house go dey called house of prayer,’ but una don make am ‘den of robbers!’”
Di blind and di lame come to am for di temple, and e heal dem.
But when di chief priests and di scribes see di wonderful things wey e do, and di pikin dem wey dey cry for di temple and dey talk say, “Hosanna to David pikin!” dem dey indignant,
and talk say to am, “You hear wetin dem dey talk?” Jesus talk say to dem, “Yes. Una never read, ‘From di mouth of babies and nursing babies you don perfect praise?’”
E leave dem, and go Bethany outside di city, and camp for dat place.
Now for morning, as e dey return to di city, e dey hungry.
As e see fig tree by di road, e come to am, and find nothing on am except leaves. E talk say to am, “Make fruit no dey from you again forever!” Immediately di fig tree wither away.
When di disciples see am, dem marvel, dey talk say, “How di fig tree take wither away immediately?”

Jesus answer dem, “Most certainly I tell una, if una get faith, and no doubt, una no go only do wetin dem do to di fig tree, but even if una talk say to dis mountain, ‘Make dem take you up and throw you enter di sea,’ dem go do am.”
“All things, whatever una ask for prayer, as una dey believe, una go receive.”
When e don enter di temple, di chief priests and di elders of di people come to am as e dey teach. Dem talk say, “By wetin authority you dey do dis things? Who give you dis authority?”
Jesus answer dem, “I too go ask una one question, wey if una tell me, I go also tell una by wetin authority I dey do dis things.”
“Di baptism of John, wia e come from? From heaven or from men?” Dem reason among demself, and talk say, “If we talk say, ‘From heaven,’ e go ask us, ‘Why den una no believe am?’”
“But if we talk say, ‘From men,’ we dey fear di multitude, because all dey hold John as prophet.”
Dem answer Jesus, and talk say, “We no know.” E talk say to dem, “I no go tell una too by wetin authority I dey do dis things.”
“But wetin una think? One man get two sons, and e come to di first, and talk say, ‘My son, go work today for my vineyard.’”
“E answer, ‘I no go,’ but afterward e change im mind, and go work.”
“E come to di second, and talk di same. E answer, ‘I dey go, oga,’ but e no go.”
“Which of di two do di will of im papa?” Dem talk say to am, “Di first.” Jesus talk say to dem, “Most certainly I tell una say di tax collectors and di prostitutes dey enter God Kingdom before una.”

“Because John come to una for di way of righteousness, and una no believe am, but di tax collectors and di prostitutes believe am. When una see am, una no even repent afterward, so that una go believe am.”
“Hear another parable. Man dey wey na oga of household, wey plant vineyard, set hedge round am, dig winepress inside am, build tower, lease am out to farmers, and leave go another country.”
“When di season for di fruit come near, e send im servants to di farmers, to receive im fruit.”
“Di farmers take im servants, beat one, kill another, and stone another.”
“Again, e send other servants more pass di first: and dem treat dem di same way.”
“But afterward e send im son to dem, and talk say, ‘Dem go respect my son.’”
“But di farmers, when dem see di son, talk say among demself, ‘Dis na di heir. Come, make we kill am, and seize im inheritance.’”
“So dem take am, and throw am out of di vineyard, and kill am.”
“So when di oga of di vineyard come, wetin e go do to dem farmers?”
Dem tell am, “E go destroy dem miserable men miserably, and e go lease out di vineyard to other farmers, wey go give am di fruit for im season.”
Jesus talk say to dem, “Una never read for di Scriptures, ‘Di stone wey di builders reject, na im dem make head of di corner. Dis come from di Lord. E dey marvelous for our eyes?’”
“So I tell una, God Kingdom go dey taken away from una, and dem go give am to nation wey go bring forth im fruit.”
“Di one wey fall on dis stone go break to pieces, but on whoever e go fall, e go scatter am like dust.”
When di chief priests and di Pharisees hear im parables, dem perceive say e dey talk about dem.
When dem seek to seize am, dem fear di multitudes, because dem consider am as prophet.
Jesus answer and talk again for parables to dem, and talk say,
“Kingdom of Heaven be like one king, wey make marriage feast for im son,”
“and send out im servants to call dem wey dem invite to di marriage feast, but dem no want come.”
“Again e send out other servants, and talk say, ‘Tell dem wey dem invite, Look, I don prepare my dinner. Dem don kill my oxen and my fat cattle, and all things don ready. Come to di marriage feast!’”
“But dem make light of am, and go dem way, one to im own farm, another to im merchandise,”
“and di rest grab im servants, mistreat dem, and kill dem.”
“But di king dey enraged, and send im armies, destroy dem murderers, and burn dem city.”
“Den e talk say to im servants, ‘Di wedding don ready, but dem wey dem invite no worthy.’”
“‘So go to di intersections of di highways, and as many as una go find, invite dem to di marriage feast.’”
“Dem servants go di highways, and gather together as many as dem find, both bad and good. Di wedding full with guests.”
“But when di king enter to see di guests, e see one man for dat place wey no wear wedding clothing,”
“and e talk say to am, ‘Friend, how you take enter here without wedding clothing?’ E no get word.”
“Den di king talk say to di servants, ‘Bind am hand and foot, carry am away, and throw am enter di outer darkness; na dat place weeping and grinding of teeth go dey.’”
“Because plenty dey called, but few dey chosen.”
Den di Pharisees leave and take counsel how dem go entrap am for im talk.

Dem send dem disciples to am, with di Herodians, and talk say, “Teacher, we know say you honest, and you dey teach di way of God for truth, no matter who you teach, because you no dey partial to anybody.”
“So tell us, wetin you think? E lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, or no?”
But Jesus perceive dem wickedness, and talk say, “Why una dey test me, una hypocrites?”
“Show me di tax money.” Dem bring one denarius to am.
E ask dem, “Na whose image and inscription dis be?”
Dem talk say to am, “Caesar own.” Den e talk say to dem, “So give to Caesar di things wey na Caesar own, and to God di things wey na God own.”
When dem hear am, dem marvel, and leave am, and go dem way.
For dat day Sadducees, dem wey dey talk say resurrection no dey, come to am. Dem ask am,
and talk say, “Teacher, Moses talk say, ‘If man die, e no get pikin, im brother go marry im wife, and raise up seed for im brother.’”
“Now seven brothers dey with us. Di first marry and die, and as e no get seed, e leave im wife to im brother.”
“For di same way di second too, and di third, reach di seventh.”
“After dem all, di woman die.”
“For di resurrection den, na who wife e go be among di seven? Because dem all get am.”
But Jesus answer dem, “Una dey mistaken, because una no know di Scriptures, and una no know di power of God.”
“Because for di resurrection dem no dey marry, and dem no dey give dem for marriage, but dem dey like God angels for heaven.”
“But about di resurrection of di dead, una never read wetin God talk to una, say,”
“‘I na di God of Abraham, and di God of Isaac, and di God of Jacob?’ God no be di God of di dead, but of di living.”
When di multitudes hear am, dem dey astonished for im teaching.
But di Pharisees, when dem hear say e don silence di Sadducees, gather demself together.
One of dem, lawyer, ask am question, dey test am.
“Teacher, which one na di greatest commandment for di law?”
Jesus talk say to am, “‘You go love di Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’”
“Dis na di first and great commandment.”
“Second one wey like am na dis, ‘You go love your neighbor as yourself.’”
“For dis two commandments di whole law and di prophets dey depend.”
Now while di Pharisees gather together, Jesus ask dem question,
and talk say, “Wetin una think about Christ? Na who pikin e be?” Dem talk say to am, “David own.”
E talk say to dem, “How den David for di Spirit dey call am Lord, say,”
“‘Di Lord talk say to my Lord, Sit for my right hand, until I make your enemies di footstool for your feet.’”
“If David den dey call am Lord, how e be im pikin?”
Nobody fit answer am one word, and nobody dare ask am any more questions from dat day forward.
Den Jesus talk to di multitudes and to im disciples,
and talk say, “Di scribes and di Pharisees dey sit for Moses seat.”
“So whatever dem tell una to observe, observe and do am, but no do dem works; because dem dey talk, and dem no dey do.”
“Because dem dey bind heavy burdens wey hard to carry, and lay dem on men shoulders; but dem demself no go lift one finger to help dem.”
“But dem dey do all dem works so that men go see dem. Dem dey make dem phylacteries broad and enlarge di fringes of dem garments.”
“Dem love di place of honor for feasts, di best seats for di synagogues,”
“di greetings for di marketplaces, and make men call dem ‘Rabbi, Rabbi.’”
“But una no make dem call una ‘Rabbi,’ because one na una teacher, Christ, and una all na brothers.”
“No call any man for di earth una papa, because one na una Papa God, di one wey dey heaven.”
“No make dem call una leaders too, because one na una leader, Christ.”
“But di one wey great pass among una go be una servant.”
“Whoever go exalt imself go dey humbled, and whoever go humble imself go dey exalted.”
“But woe dey for una, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! Because una dey shut up Kingdom of Heaven against men; because una no dey enter una self, and una no dey allow dem wey dey enter to enter.”
“Woe dey for una, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! Because una dey devour widows houses, and for pretense una dey make long prayers. So una go receive greater condemnation.”

“Woe dey for una, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! Because una dey travel round by sea and land to make one proselyte; and when e become one, una dey make am twice as much pikin of Gehenna as una self.”
“Woe dey for una, una blind guides, wey dey talk say, ‘Whoever swear by di temple, e be nothing; but whoever swear by di gold of di temple, e dey obligated.’”
“Una fools and blind! Because which one great pass, di gold, or di temple wey dey make di gold holy?”
“Una dey talk say, ‘Whoever swear by di altar, e be nothing; but whoever swear by di gift wey dey on am, e dey obligated.’”
“Una blind fools! Because which one great pass, di gift, or di altar wey dey make di gift holy?”
“So di one wey swear by di altar, swear by am, and by everything wey dey on am.”
“Di one wey swear by di temple, swear by am, and by di one wey dey live inside am.”
“Di one wey swear by heaven, swear by God throne, and by di one wey dey sit on am.”

“Woe dey for una, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! Because una dey tithe mint and anise and cumin, and una don leave undone di weightier matters of di law: justice, mercy, and faith. But una suppose do dis ones, and no leave di other undone.”
“Una blind guides, wey dey strain out gnat, and swallow camel!”
“Woe dey for una, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! Because una dey clean di outside of di cup and of di platter, but inside dem full of extortion and unrighteousness.”
“You blind Pharisee, first clean di inside of di cup and of di platter, so that di outside of am go become clean too.”
“Woe dey for una, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! Because una be like whitewashed tombs, wey outside look beautiful, but inside dem full of dead men bones and of all uncleanness.”
“Even so una too outside dey appear righteous to men, but inside una full of hypocrisy and iniquity.”
“Woe dey for una, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! Because una dey build di tombs of di prophets, and decorate di tombs of di righteous,”
“and dey talk say, ‘If we live for di days of our papa dem, we no go don join dem for di blood of di prophets.’”
“So una dey testify against una self say una na pikin dem of dem wey kill di prophets.”
“Fill up den, di measure of una papa dem.”
“Una serpents, una pikin dem of vipers, how una go escape di judgment of Gehenna?”
“So look, I send to una prophets, wise men, and scribes. Some of dem una go kill and crucify; and some of dem una go flog for una synagogues, and persecute from city to city;”
“so that on una go come all di righteous blood wey dem shed on di earth, from di blood of righteous Abel to di blood of Zachariah, Barachiah pikin, wey una kill between di sanctuary and di altar.”
“Most certainly I tell una, all dis things go come upon dis generation.”

“Jerusalem, Jerusalem, wey dey kill di prophets, and dey stone dem wey dem send to am! How often I want gather your pikin dem together, even as hen dey gather im chicks under im wings, and una no dey willing!”
“Look, dem don leave una house desolate for una.”
“Because I tell una, una no go see me from now on, until una talk say, ‘Blessed na di one wey dey come for di name of di Lord!’”
Jesus come out from di temple, and dey go im way. Im disciples come to am to show am di buildings of di temple.
But e answer dem, “Una no see all dis things? Most certainly I tell una, no one stone go remain here on another stone wey dem no go throw down.”
As e sit on di Mount of Olives, di disciples come to am privately, dey talk say, “Tell us, when dis things go be? Wetin be di sign of your coming, and of di end of di age?”
Jesus answer dem, “Make una dey careful say nobody lead una astray.”
“Because plenty go come for my name, dey talk say, ‘I na Christ,’ and dem go lead plenty astray.”
“Una go hear of wars and rumors of wars. See say una no dey troubled, because all dis must happen, but di end never reach.”
“Because nation go rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom; and famines, plagues, and earthquakes go dey for various places.”
“But all dis things na di beginning of birth pains.”
“Den dem go hand una over to oppression, and go kill una. All di nations go hate una because of my name.”
“Den plenty go stumble, and go hand over one another, and go hate one another.”
“Plenty false prophets go rise, and go lead plenty astray.”
“Because iniquity go multiply, di love of plenty go grow cold.”
“But di one wey endure to di end, na im go dey saved.”
“Dis Good News of di Kingdom go dey preached for di whole world for testimony to all di nations, and den di end go come.”
“So when una see di abomination of desolation, wey dem talk about through Daniel di prophet, dey stand for di holy place — make di reader understand —”
“Den make dem wey dey Judea run go di mountains.”
“Make di one wey dey for di housetop no come down to take out things wey dey im house.”
“Make di one wey dey for di field no return back to get im clothes.”
“But woe dey for dem wey dey pregnant and for nursing mothers for dem days!”
“Pray say una flight no go dey for winter, or on Sabbath,”
“because den great oppression go dey, wey never dey from di beginning of di world until now, no, and e no go ever dey again.”
“Unless dem shorten dem days, nobody go don dey saved. But because of di chosen ones, dem go shorten dem days.”
“Den if any man tell una, ‘Look, Christ dey here,’ or, ‘E dey for dat place,’ no believe am.”
“Because false christs, and false prophets go rise, and dem go show great signs and wonders; so as to lead astray, if e possible, even di chosen ones.”
“Look, I don tell una before.”
“If den dem tell una, ‘Look, e dey for di wilderness,’ no go out; ‘Look, e dey for di inner rooms,’ no believe am.”
“Because as lightning dey flash from di east, and dem dey see am reach di west, so di coming of Son of Man go be.”
“Because wherever di carcass dey, na for dat place di vultures go gather together.”
“But immediately after di oppression of dem days, di sun go dark, di moon no go give im light, di stars go fall from di sky, and di powers of di heavens go shake;”
“and den di sign of Son of Man go appear for di sky. Den all di tribes of di earth go mourn, and dem go see Son of Man dey come on di clouds of di sky with power and great glory.”
“E go send out im angels with great sound of trumpet, and dem go gather together im chosen ones from di four winds, from one end of di sky to di other.”
“Now from di fig tree learn dis parable. When im branch don become tender, and put forth im leaves, una know say summer near.”
“Even so una too, when una see all dis things, know say e near, even for di doors.”
“Most certainly I tell una, dis generation no go pass away, until all dis things don accomplish.”
“Heaven and earth go pass away, but my words no go pass away.”
“But nobody know dat day and hour, even di angels of heaven no know, and di Pikin no know, but Papa God only.”
“As di days of Noah be, so di coming of Son of Man go be.”
“Because as for dem days wey dey before di flood dem dey eat and drink, marry and give for marriage, until di day wey Noah enter di ark,”
“and dem no know until di flood come, and carry dem all away, so di coming of Son of Man go be.”
“Den two men go dey for di field: one go dey taken and one go dey left;”
“two women dey grind for di mill, one go dey taken and one go dey left.”
“So watch, because una no know for wetin hour una Lord dey come.”
“But know dis, say if di oga of di house know for wetin watch of di night di thief dey come, e for watch, and e no for allow dem break into im house.”
“So una too make una ready, because for hour wey una no expect, Son of Man go come.”
“Who den be di faithful and wise servant, wey im oga don set over im household, to give dem dem food for di right season?”
“Blessed na dat servant wey im oga go find dey do so when e come.”
“Most certainly I tell una say e go set am over all wey e get.”
“But if dat evil servant talk for im heart, ‘My oga dey delay im coming,’”
“and begin to beat im fellow servants, and eat and drink with di drunk people;”
“di oga of dat servant go come for day wey e no expect, and for hour wey e no know am,”
“and go cut am in pieces, and appoint im portion with di hypocrites. Weeping and di gnashing of teeth go dey for dat place.”
“Den Kingdom of Heaven go be like ten virgins, wey take dem lamps, and come out to meet di bridegroom.”
“Five of dem dey foolish, and five dey wise.”
“Dem wey foolish take dem lamps, and no take oil with dem,”
“but di wise take oil inside dem vessels with dem lamps.”
“Now while di bridegroom delay, dem all dey slumber and sleep.”
“But for midnight, cry come, ‘Look! Di bridegroom dey come! Come out to meet am!’”
“Den all dem virgins rise, and trim dem lamps.”
“Di foolish talk say to di wise, ‘Give us some of your oil, because our lamps dey go out.’”
“But di wise answer, and talk say, ‘Wetin go happen if e no enough for us and una? Una go better go to dem wey dey sell, and buy for una self.’”
“While dem dey go buy, di bridegroom come, and dem wey ready enter with am go di marriage feast, and dem shut di door.”
“Afterward di other virgins come too, dey talk say, ‘Lord, Lord, open for us.’”
“But e answer, ‘Most certainly I tell una, I no know una.’”
“So watch, because una no know di day or di hour wey Son of Man dey come.”
“Because e be like man wey dey go to another country, wey call im own servants, and hand im goods to dem.”
“To one e give five talents, to another two, to another one; to each according to im own ability. Den e go im journey.”
“Immediately di one wey receive di five talents trade with dem, and make another five talents.”
“For like manner di one wey get di two gain another two.”
“But di one wey receive di one leave and dig for di earth, and hide im oga money.”
“Now after long time di oga of dem servants come, and settle accounts with dem.”
“Di one wey receive di five talents come and bring another five talents, dey talk say, ‘Oga, you hand over five talents to me. Look, I don gain another five talents beside dem.’”
“Im oga talk say to am, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant. You don dey faithful over few things, I go set you over plenty things. Enter di joy of your oga.’”
“Di one wey get di two talents come too and talk say, ‘Oga, you hand over two talents to me. Look, I don gain another two talents beside dem.’”
“Im oga talk say to am, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant. You don dey faithful over few things, I go set you over plenty things. Enter di joy of your oga.’”
“Di one wey receive di one talent come too and talk say, ‘Oga, I know you say you na hard man, dey reap wia you no sow, and dey gather wia you no scatter.’”
“‘I fear, and I leave and hide your talent for di earth. Look, you get wetin na your own.’”
“But im oga answer am, ‘You wicked and slothful servant. You know say I dey reap wia I no sow, and gather wia I no scatter.’”
“‘So you suppose deposit my money with di bankers, and when I come I for receive back my own with interest.’”
“‘So take away di talent from am, and give am to di one wey get di ten talents.’”
“‘Because to everyone wey get dem go give, and e go get abundance, but from di one wey no get, even wetin e get dem go take away.’”
“‘Throw out di unprofitable servant enter di outer darkness, wia weeping and gnashing of teeth go dey.’”
“But when Son of Man come for im glory, and all di holy angels with am, den e go sit for di throne of im glory.”
“Before am all di nations go gather, and e go separate dem one from another, as shepherd dey separate di sheep from di goats.”
“E go set di sheep for im right hand, but di goats for di left.”
“Den di King go tell dem wey dey im right hand, ‘Come, una wey my Papa God don bless, inherit di Kingdom wey dem prepare for una from di foundation of di world;’”
“‘because I dey hungry, and una give me food to eat; I dey thirsty, and una give me drink; I na stranger, and una take me in;’”
“‘naked, and una clothe me; I dey sick, and una visit me; I dey for prison, and una come to me.’”
“Den di righteous go answer am, dey talk say, ‘Lord, when we see you hungry, and feed you; or thirsty, and give you drink?’”
“‘When we see you as stranger, and take you in; or naked, and clothe you?’”
“‘When we see you sick, or for prison, and come to you?’”
“Di King go answer dem, ‘Most certainly I tell una, as much as una do am to one of di least of dem my brothers, una do am to me.’”
“Den e go talk too to dem wey dey left hand, ‘Depart from me, una wey dem curse, enter di fire wey no dey end wey dem prepare for di devil and im angels;’”
“‘because I dey hungry, and una no give me food to eat; I dey thirsty, and una give me no drink;’”
“‘I na stranger, and una no take me in; naked, and una no clothe me; sick, and for prison, and una no visit me.’”
“Den dem too go answer, dey talk say, ‘Lord, when we see you hungry, or thirsty, or stranger, or naked, or sick, or for prison, and no help you?’”
“Den e go answer dem, dey talk say, ‘Most certainly I tell una, as much as una no do am to one of di least of dem, una no do am to me.’”
“Dis ones go go away enter punishment wey no dey end, but di righteous go enter life wey no dey end.”
